title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing, fairness, starvation prevention, timeouts
author: Alyssa Chen
description: Context: the continuous-batcher scheduler previously exhibited queue head starvation under high-concurrency workloads and suboptimal fairness when mixing short/long sequences. This caused tail latency regressions for low-token requests and increased KV cache thrashing. Motivation: improve overall latency SLO compliance and reduce 99th percentile spikes by adding bounded queueing, per-client fairness tokens, starvation prevention, and operation-level timeouts. Changes: 1) Introduced a bounded FIFO hold queue with adaptive admission based on recent service time distributions; 2) Per-client fairness tokens that ensure short-request priority without starving heavy users; 3) Starvation prevention timer: tasks in queue beyond threshold are promoted with exponential priority boost; 4) Operation timeouts for long-running scheduling decisions to avoid head-of-line blocking; 5) KV cache affinity hinting to colocate likely reused KV entries and reduce remote cache misses; 6) New unit and integration tests (scheduler deterministic replay, multi-client fairness scenarios) and updated perf canary harness. Related: addresses ENG-1024, follows discussion in ENG-1102 and benchmarks in /benchmark-lab. Checklist: [x] design doc linked; [x] unit tests added; [x] integration tests added; [x] perf numbers validated; [x] docs updated for scheduler tunables. Notes: algorithm parameters are exposed under continuous_batcher.scheduling.*, defaulted conservatively to avoid regressions and can be tuned via env/console. See inline notes in code for rationale and microbench results.

release_notes: Scheduler: improve fairness and starvation prevention for continuous batching; add bounded hold queue, per-client fairness tokens, starvation promotion timer, and scheduling timeouts. Exposes new tuning keys under continuous_batcher.scheduling.*. Improves 99th percentile latency for mixed short/long request workloads.
notes_for_ops: Deploy notes: defaults are conservative; recommend canary rollout to Dedicated clusters then scale to Hosted. Monitor continuous_batcher.scheduler.promotions and continuous_batcher.queue.depth metrics. If regressions observed, reduce admission rate or lower promotion multiplier.
